memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The Egyptians pursued them, and all Pharaoh's horses and chariots and horsemen
followed them into the sea." - Ex 14:23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One short verse, and it is astonishing.

They saw a sea standing up in two walls of water. They saw a supernatural act
that no army in history had encountered. And they drove their chariots straight
in.

How? Because a hardened heart does not reason well. Pharaoh's army had already
watched their nation destroyed by ten plagues and learned nothing. Evidence had
stopped working on them a long time ago.

This is one of Scripture's sober warnings. Hardness is not a lack of information.
Jesus said of the rich man's brothers, "If they do not listen to Moses and the
Prophets, they will not be convinced even if someone rises from the dead" (Luke
16:31). And when Jesus did rise, many were not convinced.

We sometimes imagine that if God gave a clear enough sign, people would believe.
Egypt had signs upon signs. The problem was never the evidence.

That is why we pray for people rather than merely arguing with them. Only God
softens a heart. Ezekiel spoke of God removing a heart of stone and giving a
heart of flesh (Ezek 36:26). That is His work, and it is worth asking Him for.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there an area where you have stopped responding to what God has clearly
   shown you?
2. Who are you arguing with that you should be praying for?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, keep my heart soft toward You. Where I have grown resistant, break through
gently, and soften the hearts of those I love. Amen.
